audit_status.source_base: Greek Hebrews text tradition with priesthood and Psalm citation texture; draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for high priest taken from humans, Melchizedek citation, learned obedience, milk/solid food warning.

verses.restored: For every high priest taken from humans is appointed on behalf of humans in things toward the Divine, so that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices concerning sins/misalignments,

familiar.text: For every high priest taken from among men is ordained for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins:

modern.text: Every high priest is appointed from among men to represent them in matters relating to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.

original.text: Πᾶς γὰρ ἀρχιερεὺς ἐξ ἀνθρώπων λαμβανόμενος ὑπὲρ ἀνθρώπων καθίσταται τὰ πρὸς τὸν θεόν, ἵνα προσφέρῃ δῶρά τε καὶ θυσίας ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν,

verses.restored: being able to deal gently with the ignorant and wandering, since he himself is also surrounded with weakness.

familiar.text: Who can have compassion on the ignorant, and on them that are out of the way; for that he himself also is compassed with infirmity.

modern.text: He is able to deal gently with those who are ignorant and misguided, since he himself is beset by weakness.

original.text: μετριοπαθεῖν δυνάμενος τοῖς ἀγνοοῦσι καὶ πλανωμένοις ἐπεὶ καὶ αὐτὸς περίκειται ἀσθένειαν,

verses.restored: And because of this he owes, just as concerning the people, so also concerning himself, to offer for sins/misalignments.

familiar.text: And by reason hereof he ought, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins.

modern.text: That is why he is obligated to offer sacrifices for his own sins, as well as for the sins of the people.

original.text: καὶ ⸂διʼ αὐτὴν⸃ ὀφείλει, καθὼς περὶ τοῦ λαοῦ, οὕτως καὶ περὶ ⸀αὑτοῦ προσφέρειν ⸀περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν.

verses.restored: And no one takes the honor to oneself, but being called by the Divine, just as Aaron also.

familiar.text: And no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron.

modern.text: No one takes this honor upon himself; he must be called by God, just as Aaron was.

original.text: καὶ οὐχ ἑαυτῷ τις λαμβάνει τὴν τιμήν, ἀλλὰ καλούμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ⸀καθώσπερ καὶ Ἀαρών.

verses.restored: So also Messiah did not glorify himself to become high priest, but the One speaking to him: You are my Son; today I have begotten you.

familiar.text: So also Christ glorified not himself to be made an high priest; but he that said unto him, Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee.

modern.text: So also Christ did not take upon Himself the glory of becoming a high priest, but He was called by the One who said to Him: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.”

original.text: Οὕτως καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς οὐχ ἑαυτὸν ἐδόξασεν γενηθῆναι ἀρχιερέα, ἀλλʼ ὁ λαλήσας πρὸς αὐτόν· Υἱός μου εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε·

verses.restored: Just as also in another place he says: You are priest into the age according to the order of Melchizedek.

familiar.text: As he saith also in another place, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.

modern.text: And in another passage God says: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”

original.text: καθὼς καὶ ἐν ἑτέρῳ λέγει· Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ,

verses.restored: Who in the days of his flesh, with loud cries and tears, having offered petitions and supplications to the One able to save/heal him out of death, and being heard because of reverent devotion,

familiar.text: Who in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him that was able to save him from death, and was heard in that he feared;

modern.text: During the days of Jesus’ earthly life, He offered up prayers and petitions with loud cries and tears to the One who could save Him from death, and He was heard because of His reverence.

original.text: ὃς ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ δεήσεις τε καὶ ἱκετηρίας πρὸς τὸν δυνάμενον σῴζειν αὐτὸν ἐκ θανάτου μετὰ κραυγῆς ἰσχυρᾶς καὶ δακρύων προσενέγκας καὶ εἰσακουσθεὶς ἀπὸ τῆς εὐλαβείας,

verses.restored: though being Son, learned obedience from what he suffered,

familiar.text: Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered;

modern.text: Although He was a Son, He learned obedience from what He suffered.

original.text: καίπερ ὢν υἱός, ἔμαθεν ἀφʼ ὧν ἔπαθεν τὴν ὑπακοήν,

verses.restored: and having been completed, became cause/source of age-long salvation/healing to all those obeying him,

familiar.text: And being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him;

modern.text: And having been made perfect, He became the source of eternal salvation to all who obey Him

original.text: καὶ τελειωθεὶς ἐγένετο ⸂πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπακούουσιν αὐτῷ⸃ αἴτιος σωτηρίας αἰωνίου,

verses.restored: being addressed by the Divine as high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.

familiar.text: Called of God an high priest after the order of Melchisedec.

modern.text: and was designated by God as high priest in the order of Melchizedek. Milk and Solid Food (1 Corinthians 3:1–9)

original.text: προσαγορευθεὶς ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἀρχιερεὺς κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ.

verses.restored: Concerning whom the word for us is much and hard to explain, since you have become sluggish in hearing.

familiar.text: Of whom we have many things to say, and hard to be uttered, seeing ye are dull of hearing.

modern.text: We have much to say about this, but it is hard to explain, because you are dull of hearing.

original.text: Περὶ οὗ πολὺς ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος καὶ δυσερμήνευτος λέγειν, ἐπεὶ νωθροὶ γεγόνατε ταῖς ἀκοαῖς·

verses.restored: For indeed, though owing to be teachers by reason of time, again you have need for someone to teach you the beginning elements of the oracles of the Divine, and you have become having need of milk, not solid food.

familiar.text: For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat.

modern.text: Although by this time you ought to be teachers, you need someone to reteach you the basic principles of God’s word. You need milk, not solid food!

original.text: καὶ γὰρ ὀφείλοντες εἶναι διδάσκαλοι διὰ τὸν χρόνον, πάλιν χρείαν ἔχετε τοῦ διδάσκειν ὑμᾶς ⸀τινὰ τὰ στοιχεῖα τῆς ἀρχῆς τῶν λογίων τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ γεγόνατε χρείαν ἔχοντες γάλακτος, ⸀οὐ στερεᾶς τροφῆς.

verses.restored: For everyone sharing milk is inexperienced in word of righteousness/justice, for one is infant.

familiar.text: For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.

modern.text: For everyone who lives on milk is still an infant, inexperienced in the message of righteousness.

original.text: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ μετέχων γάλακτος ἄπειρος λόγου δικαιοσύνης, νήπιος γάρ ἐστιν·

verses.restored: But solid food is for mature ones, those having faculties trained through practice for discernment of both beautiful/good and harmful.

familiar.text: But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.

modern.text: But solid food is for the mature, who by constant use have trained their senses to distinguish good from evil.

original.text: τελείων δέ ἐστιν ἡ στερεὰ τροφή, τῶν διὰ τὴν ἕξιν τὰ αἰσθητήρια γεγυμνασμένα ἐχόντων πρὸς διάκρισιν καλοῦ τε καὶ κακοῦ.

translation_notes: High priesthood begins in gentle solidarity with weakness, not status elevation.
Melchizedek language should be handled as Psalm/canonical argument, not speculative overreach.
Jesus learning obedience through suffering must not romanticize harm; it names faithful embodiment under pressure.
safety_note: The milk/solid-food warning is communal exhortation toward discernment, not contempt for beginners.
